**Verdict:** REVISE
**Lens:** Methodology

**Findings:**

1. Severity: Nit — **Regex correctness traces clean for the incident shape.** Tracing `\b[A-Z]\s*(?:->|→)\s*[A-Z](?:_[a-z]+)?\b` against `"B->S_single"`: `\b` at start, `B` (uppercase), `->` (ASCII arrow, `\s*` matches empty), `S` (uppercase), `_single` (optional `_[a-z]+` group), `\b` before end-of-string. Match = `"B->S_single"`. Same for `"S->D_multi"`, `"D->R_single"`. For `"D->R_single/multi"`: matches `"D->R_single"`; second attempt anchored at `M` fails because next char `u` is lowercase, so `/multi` tail is ignored (acceptable — one hit per token is enough to WARN). Unicode arrow `S→D` and spaced `A -> B` both trace clean. Positive AC-1 is sound. — Resolution: none; note in test comment that only the first LHS→RHS pair per token is captured, sufficient for WARN semantics.

2. Severity: **Must-Fix** — **Sidecar false-positive envelope is unbounded and unaddressed.** The plan's scope caveat handles PROSE false positives (methodology text like "we compared A → B") via the check-28 figure-only scoping, but figure sidecars themselves routinely carry legitimate single-letter arrow constructions the new regex will WARN on: chemistry reaction axes (`"H->O"`, `"A->B"` in a reaction-graph figure), transition matrices with single-letter state labels (`"X -> Y"` in an HMM/Markov figure), enum axis labels. None of these are opaque codes — they're legitimate LEGENDS in a figure sidecar. The incident tokens `"B->S_single"`/`"D->R_multi"` are opaque BECAUSE they compress an unexplained multi-word decoding into single letters + snake slugs; a bare `"H->O"` labeling reactant→product is not the same class. The plan pins only ONE negative (`"Fe->Fe2+"` multi-char) but leaves single-letter chemistry / state-machine labels flagged as false positives. Given the always-on `.claude/rules/code-style.md` fail-fast rule and this project's mixed figure catalog (chemistry cross-refs appear in mentor-update figures), the false-positive rate matters. — Resolution: EITHER (a) narrow the regex to REQUIRE the `_[a-z]+` suffix on the RHS (`\b[A-Z]\s*(?:->|→)\s*[A-Z]_[a-z]+\b`) — matches exactly the incident shape (letter → letter + snake), rejects bare `H->O` / `A->B`; document that a bare-letter arrow is legitimate legend syntax and out of scope; OR (b) keep the current regex but add a pinned false-positive negative test set (`"H->O"`, `"A->B"`, `"X -> Y"`) and an EXPLICIT plan clause accepting these WARNs as tolerable given the incident weight. (a) is preferable — the incident shape is specific and narrowing preserves signal; (b) shifts noise onto every future single-letter-arrow legend author.

3. Severity: Concern — **`_SNAKE_TOKEN_RE` interaction analysis is correct but under-tested.** The classifier suppresses `S_single` (1 underscore, no digit) per L8815-8817; casefold-dedup on `"B->S_single"` vs. a hypothetical `S_single` snake hit is moot because snake is suppressed. Correct. But this interaction is fragile: any future loosening of `_SNAKE_TOKEN_RE`'s suppression (e.g. flagging 1-segment digit-free snakes) would introduce a dedup collision where `"B->S_single"` and `"S_single"` both hit and the casefold seen-set drops one. — Resolution: add ONE regression test asserting `_opaque_code_tokens("B->S_single")` returns EXACTLY `["B->S_single"]` (length 1, exact string), not `["B->S_single", "S_single"]`, to lock the current interaction. Cheap insurance against a future snake-regex loosening.

4. Severity: Concern — **AC-4 integration test is thin vs. incumbent coverage.** The H-code / slot-family / candidate classes each carry both a classifier unit test (direct `_opaque_code_tokens(...)` assertion) AND a full-body walker test (sha-pinned figure + sidecar → WARN + token in `res.detail`). The plan pins AC-1/2/3 at the classifier level and AC-4 at the walker level with ONE fixture. Missing: a walker test asserting that the letter-arrow token appears in `res.detail` alongside path exemption (i.e. a figure whose title carries `"B->S_single"` AND whose filename is `figures/issue_1902/A->B.png` — the exemption applies to the FILENAME token, the title token still WARNs). Without this the path-exemption + walker-integration surface is only mock-tested. — Resolution: extend AC-4 to two fixtures — (i) title-only letter-arrow → WARN, (ii) title letter-arrow + path-word letter-arrow in filename → WARN with only the title token in `res.detail` (path token exempted). Mirrors the incumbent classes' walker coverage.

5. Severity: Concern — **Scope discipline: the plan closes the letter-arrow class but does not audit sibling escape paths.** Docstring residuals (i)/(ii)/(iii) name three known check-28 walker gaps: pre-`meta["text"]` sidecar blindness, whitespace-free column KEYs unscanned, path-shaped exemption over-broad. Could a letter-arrow string still evade the new regex via any of these? (ii) is directly relevant: if a future figure sidecar exposes a DataFrame column KEY (not a value) containing `"B->S_single"`, the walker skips whitespace-free column keys entirely — the new regex would never see it. Not an in-scope fix (the plan is narrowly a regex-add), but the plan does not NAME this residual gap in its scope caveat. — Resolution: add a one-line scope caveat to the plan body: "Closes the classifier gap for `meta['text']`-echoed sidecar strings; the docstring's residual (ii) whitespace-free column-KEY gap remains a separate future fix and could still admit letter-arrow strings via DataFrame column keys." Documents the known-unknown without expanding scope.
